content.overview: Members act in general meeting by ordinary or special resolution, on notice, with the statutory quorum.
content.glance: Members act in general meeting by ordinary or special resolution, on notice, with the statutory quorum.
content.study: AGM business includes adoption of accounts, declaration of dividend, appointment of directors and auditors. Other business is special and needs an explanatory statement. A special resolution needs a 75 per cent majority of votes cast and notice specifying the intention. Certain resolutions must be filed under s. 117. A resolution may be passed by postal ballot under s. 110 for notified matters.

caseLaw.name: Foss v Harbottle
caseLaw.point: The company is the proper plaintiff for a wrong done to the company. A member cannot sue for a reflective loss except within the statutory exceptions, now including section 241 and section 245.
